expression: Annual eligible contract value per client × potential eligible clients
original_wording:
Total Addressable Market = Annual Contract Value per client x Number of potential clients
Market size of a product/service in value that the company can achieve

expression: Promoter percentage − detractor percentage
original_wording:
Net Promoter Score = % of Promoters - % of Detractors
Measures customer satisfaction and loyalty

expression: Sales on the quota basis / quota on the same basis × 100
original_wording:
Sales Attainment = Monthly Sales / Monthly Quota
% of quota attained by sales team

expression: Σ (deal valueᵢ × compatible close probabilityᵢ)
original_wording:
Weighted Pipeline = Total deals value in pipeline x percentage close likelihood
The value of the deals in your pipeline, adjusted for the close likelihood

expression: (Opening inventory + closing inventory) / 2
original_wording:
Average Inventory = (Beginning Inventory + Ending Inventory) / 2
Amount of inventory a company has on-hand during a period

expression: Average inventory / period COGS × period days
original_wording:
Days on Hand (DoH) = (Average Inventory for period / CoGS for period) x 365
DoH is the average days before inventory is sold

expression: Stated inventory value / matching sales value
original_wording:
Stock to Sales Ratio = Inventory value / Sales value
Is the measurement of the inventory amount in storage versus the number of sales

expression: (Service + risk + capital + storage costs) / stated inventory value
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Cost of Carry = (Inventory Service Costs + Inventory Risk Costs + Capital Cost + Storage Cost) / Total Inventory Value
Percentage of total inventory value a company pays to maintain inventory in storage

expression: Undeliverable orders / total relevant orders
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Backorder Rate = Number of Undeliverable Orders / Total Number of Orders
Tracks the number of delayed orders due to stockouts

expression: Units sold / units received
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Sell-through Rate = Number of units sold / Number of units received
Comparison of the inventory amount sold and the amount of inventory received from a manufacturer

expression: Period scrap expense / average inventory value
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Scrap Rate = Scrap expenses over the period / Average inventory over the period
Measures the quality of the inventory and is used to decrease the non quality costs

expression: Validation time + recording time + storage-preparation time
original_wording:
Time to receive = Time for stock validation + Time to add stock to records + Time to prep stock for storage
Measures the effeciency of stock receiving process

expression: Book inventory value − physical inventory value
original_wording:
Inventory Shrinkage = Ending inventory value - Physically counted inventory value
Measures the shrinkage due to damage, miscounts and fraud

expression: Unsellable relevant stock / total relevant available stock
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Dead Stock = Amount of unsellable stock in period / Amount of available stock in period
Dead stock inventory no one wants to buy. Measures efficiency of supply chain

expression: Assets = liabilities + equity
original_wording: Assets = Liabilities + Owners EquityBoth tangible and intangible = amounts owed to creditors (capped) - amounts owed to owners (uncapped)

expression: Assets = liabilities + equity; closing retained earnings = opening retained earnings + attributable profit − distributions ± applicable adjustments
units: currency at a date / over a period
original_wording: Cumulative values as of a specific point in time, ie. snapshot.Assets must always = liabilities + owners equity (no exception).Retained earnings balance come from last period's balance + this month's net income on P&L.

expression: Assets = liabilities + equity
original_wording: Always ensure that assets = liabilities + equity

expression: Recognized revenue and other income − all applicable expenses
original_wording: Net income = Total Revenue - Total Expenses

expression: Relevant net sales − cost of goods/services sold
original_wording:
Gross Profit = Total Revenue - Cost of Goods Sold (CoGs)
How much is left after each sales.

expression: Net income + income tax expense + interest expense + depreciation + amortisation
original_wording:
EBITDA = Net Income + Interest Rxpense - Interest Income + Taxes + Depreciation + Amortisation
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation

expression: Gross profit − applicable operating expenses
original_wording:
Net Operating Income = Gross Profit - Operating Expenses
The profit derived from a company's regular business activities.

expression: Other income − other expenses
original_wording:
Net Other Income = Other Income - Other Expense
The net profitability of your other income / expense items, not related to your core business.

expression: Net income / matching revenue
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Net Income margin = Net Income / Revenue
Percentage of revenue that remains after deducting all expenses, including taxes and interest.

expression: Total debt / total equity
original_wording:
Debt-to-Equity Ratio = Total Debt / Total Equity
Amount of debt a company has in relation to its equity. The lower the ratio, the less the debt compared to its equity.

expression: Total debt / total assets
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Debt-to-Assets Ratio = Total Debt / Total Asset
Amount of debt a company has in relation to its assets. The lower the ration, the less the debt compared to assets.

expression: Current assets / current liabilities
original_wording:
Current Ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities
Measures whether a company has enough short-term assets to cover its short-term liabilities. The higher the ratio, the more assets you have in relation to your liabilities.

expression: Total assets / total equity
original_wording:
Equity Multiplier = Total Assets / Total Equity
Measures the proportion of a company's assets that are financed through debt versus equity. A high equity multiplier means the company is relying more on debt to finance it's assets rather than equity.

expression: (Current assets − inventory − prepayments − other non-quick current assets) / current liabilities
original_wording:
Quick Ratio = (Current Assets - Inventory) / Current Liabilities
Shows the ability of a company to meet its short-term obligations with its most liquid assets. The high the ratio, the more liquidity your business has.

expression: Cash and cash equivalents / current liabilities
original_wording:
Cash Ratio = Cash and Cash Equivalent / Current Liabilities
Amount of cash and equivalents a company has in relation to its current liabilities. The higher the ratio, the more cash you have in comparison with your current liabilities.

expression: Current assets − current liabilities
original_wording:
Net Working capital = Current Assets - Current Liabilities
Short-term liquidity and its ability to meet its current obligations. Higher NWC indicates that the company has a comfortable cushion of liquid assets to cover its short-term liabilities.

measure: Net working capital to total assets
expression: (Current assets − current liabilities) / total assets
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Net Working Capital Ratio = (Current Assets - Current Liabilities) / Total Assets
Showcases the difference between a company's current asset and its current liabilities. The higher the ratio, the more current assets you have compared to your current liabilities.

expression: Debt / (debt + equity)
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Total Debt-to-Capitalisation Ratio = Total Debt / (Total Debt + Shareholders' Equity)
The total amount of debt in relation to a company's total capitalisation (debt & equity). The lower ratio, the less your business is captailised using debt.

measure: Liabilities to adjusted tangible net worth
expression: Total liabilities / (equity − intangibles − prepayments − related-party receivables)
original_wording:
Tangible Net Worth Ratio = Total Liabilities / (Total Equity - Intangible Assets - Prepaid Assets - Due from Related Parties)
The value of all your assets and the size of all your liabilities

expression: (Eligible Tier 1 capital + eligible Tier 2 capital) / risk-weighted assets × 100
original_wording:
Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) = (Tier 1 Capital + Tier 2 Capital) / (Risk-Weighted Assets) x 100
Not liquid assets but bookkeeping of assets and liability

expression: Net income / average total assets
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Return on Assets (RoA) = Net Income / Average Total Assets
Amount of net income a company generates in relation to its total assets. The higher your RoA, the better your return on your assets.

expression: Attributable net income / average corresponding equity
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Return on Equity (RoE) = Net Income / Average Shareholders' Equity
Amount of net income a company generates in relation to its equity. The higher your RoE, the better return you are getting on your equity.

expression: Net sales / average total assets
original_wording:
Total Asset Turnover = Net Sales - Average Total Assets
A company generates for each dollar of total assets it holds. Higher TAT suggests that the company is generating more sales relative to its investment in assets.

expression: Net credit sales / average trade receivables
original_wording:
Accounts Receivables Turnover = Net Credit Sales / Average Accounts Receivable
Measures how quickly a company collects outstanding debts from customers

expression: Credit purchases / average trade payables
original_wording:
Accounts Payable Turnover = Total Supplier Purchases / Average Accounts Payable
Measures how quickly a company pays its suppliers

expression: Cost of goods sold / average inventory
original_wording:
Inventory Turnover = CoGS / Average Inventory
Meassures the number of times inventory is sold and replaced during a period

expression: Revenue / average net fixed assets
original_wording:
Fixed Asset Turnover = Revenue / Net Fixed Assets
Measures how effectively a company uses its fixed assets to generate sales

expression: Gross profit / matching net sales
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Gross Profit Margin = Gross Profit / Net Sales
% of revenue that exceeds the CoGS.

expression: Defined period net profit / defined investment base
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Return on Investment (RoI) = Net Profit / Total Investment
The return on investment capital invested in a business.

expression: Compatible operating profit / stated capital employed
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Return on Capital Employed (RoCE) = Operating Profit / Capital Employed
A company's ability to generate profits from the capital its has invested in its business.

expression: (Attributable net income − applicable preferred dividends) / weighted-average common shares
original_wording:
Earnings Per Share (EPS) = (Net Income - Preferred Dividends) / Weighted Average Shares Outstanding
The portion of a company's profit allocated to each outstanding share of common stock.

expression: Operating profit / matching revenue
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Operating Profit Margin = Operating Profit / Revenue
% of revenue that remains after deducting operating expenses.

expression: Annual dividend per corresponding share / market price per share
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Dividend Yield = Annual Dividend per Share / Market Price per Share
Return on investment from dividends

expression: (Revenue − corresponding cost of sales) / revenue
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Gross Margin Ratio = (Revenue - CoGS) / Revenue
Measures the profitablity of a company's products or services

expression: ROE = (net income / net sales) × (net sales / average total assets) × (average total assets / average equity)
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording: Dupont Analysis = Net Profit Margin, Profitability (Gross Profit Margin, Operating Profit Margin, Pre-tax Profit Margin, Effective Tax Rate) x Asset Turnover, Efficiency (Fixed Asset Turnover, AR Turnover, AP Turnover, Inventory Turnover) x Financial Leverage (Debt Ratio, Equity Ratio)

expression: Corresponding dividends / corresponding earnings
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording: Dividend Payout Ratio = Dividends / net income

expression: EBITDA / compatible interest expense
original_wording: Interest Coverage = EBITDA / Interest Expense

expression: EBITDA / (scheduled principal + compatible interest)
original_wording: Debt Service Coverage = EBITDA / (Principal + Interest)
Fixed Charged Coverage = (EBITDA + Fixed Charges - Cash Taxes - Unfunded CAPEX - Shareholder Distribution) / (P + I + Fixed Charges)

expression: Defined funded debt / compatible EBITDA
original_wording: Funded Debt to EBITDA = Total Financed Debt / EBITDA

expression: Opening-cohort customers lost during period / customers at period start
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Customer Churn Rate = Customers lost / Total Customers
Percentage of customers lost in a given time frame

expression: (New buyers this period − new buyers prior period) / new buyers prior period
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
New Buyer Growth Rate = (New buyers this month - New buyers last month) / New buyers last month
Speed at which you gain new customers over defined periods of time

expression: Revenue per customer per period × expected customer lifespan in periods
original_wording:
Lifetime Value = Customer Value x Average Customer Lifespan
Revenue from a customer over the retention time period

expression: Attributed sales and marketing cost / matching new customers acquired
original_wording:
Customer Acquisition Costs = Cost of Sales and Marketing / Number of New Customers Acquired
Amount of money a company spends to get a new customer

expression: Period revenue / stated matching customer base
original_wording:
Average Revenue per User = Total Revenue / Total number of customers
Average revenue generated per customer (either monthy or annually)

expression: (New MRR + expansion MRR) / (churned MRR + contraction MRR)
original_wording:
SaaS Quick Ratio = (Net Monthly Recurring Revenue period [MRRt] + Expansion MRRt) / (Churned MRRt + Contraction MRRt)
Compares revenue added (new business) vs. revenue lost (churn)

expression: Eligible customers × average normalized monthly recurring amount
original_wording:
Monthly Recurring Revenue = Number of customers x Average billed amount
Monthly revenue from customers with a subscription

measure: Net revenue retention for an opening cohort
expression: (Opening-cohort MRR + expansion − contraction − churn) / opening-cohort MRR × 100
original_wording:
Net Dollar Retention = Net Revenue / Opening MRR
The amount being retained from a customer or cohort over a specific period of time

expression: CAC per acquired customer / gross profit per customer per period
original_wording:
CAC Paybank = Customer Acquisition Cost / Gross Profit
Period of time till you make back your CAC

expression: Total annualized eligible contract value / eligible contract count
original_wording:
Average Contract Value = Total Revenue / No. of Contracts
The average contract value from a customer (more common in B2B)

expression: Sum of positive recurring-value increases for continuing customers
original_wording:
Expansion Revenue = (Total Revenue in Current Period - Total Revenue in Previous Period) - (Reactivation Revenue + Churn Revenue)
Added revenue from recurring customers

expression: Sum of partial recurring-value reductions for continuing customers
original_wording:
Contraction revenue = (Total Revenue in Previous Period - Total Revenue in Current Period) + Downgrade Revenue + Churn Revenue
Reduced revenue from recurring customers

expression: Attainment = actual / budget; variance rate = (actual − budget) / budget
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Budget Attainment = Budget variance / Budget Amount
% of your budget achieved

expression: Period revenue / stated matching user base
original_wording:
Average Revenue per User = Total Revenue / No. of User
The average revenue you are generating from a user (more common in B2C)

expression: Closing cash = opening cash + operating + investing + financing cash flows + applicable reconciling effects
original_wording: Ending cash = Beginning Cash + Cash from Operating Activities + Cash from Investing Activities + Cash from Finance Activities

expression: Net income + signed noncash adjustments − increase in noncash operating working capital + other required operating reconciliations
original_wording:
Operating Cash Flow (OCF) = Net Income + Depreciation + Amortisation + Other Non-Cash Items - Changes in Working Capital
A measure of a company's cash inflow and outflow from its primary business activities. A higher OCF indicates that a company has more cash available for its day-to-day operations, investments, and debt repayments.

expression: Operating + investing + financing cash flows
original_wording:
Net Cash Flow = Operating Cash Flow + Investing Cash Flow + Financing Cash Flow
The total amount of cash generated or used by a company from its operating, investing, and financing activities. Positive cash flow indicates that a company is generating more cash than it is using.

measure: Operating cash flow less capital expenditure
expression: Operating cash flow − cash CAPEX
original_wording:
Free Cash Flow (FCF) = Operating Cash Flow - Capital Expenditures
Free cash flow measures a company's cash flow available for distribution to its investors or for future investments. A positive FCF indicates that a company is generating cash from its operations and co-invest in new projects, pay dividents, or reduce debt.

measure: Free cash flow to the firm: operating-profit bridge
expression: EBIT × (1 − tax rate) + noncash operating charges − CAPEX − increase in noncash operating working capital
original_wording:
Unlevered Free Cash Flow = EBIT (1 - Tax Rate) + Depreciation & Amortization - Capital Expenditures - Changes in Working Capital
It represents the cash generated by a company's core operations that is available to all investors, regardless of its capital structure. A higher UFCF indicates that the company is generating more cash from its core operations.

measure: Free cash flow to equity: full earnings bridge
expression: Net income + noncash charges − CAPEX − increase in noncash operating working capital + net borrowing
original_wording:
Levered Free Cash Flow = EBITDA - Taxes - Capital Expenditures - Interest Expense
The cash flow available to equity shareholders after deducting interest payments on debt and incorporating any net borrowings. Higher LFCF indicates that the company has strong cash flow available to its equity shareholders even after servicing its debt.

measure: Operating cash flow: reconcile working-capital signs
expression: Net income + signed noncash adjustments − increase in noncash operating working capital + required operating reconciliations
original_wording: Operating Cash Flow = Net Income + Depreciation and Amortisation + Non-cash Items + Changes in Net Working Capital

expression: Cash investing receipts − cash investing payments
original_wording: Investing Cash Flow = Net Capital Expenditures (CAPEX)

expression: Debt proceeds − principal repayments + equity proceeds − share repurchases − distributions + other financing flows
original_wording: Financing Cash Flow = Net Debt Process + Net Equity Proceeds

expression: Operating cash flow − cash CAPEX + compatible after-tax interest adjustment
original_wording: Free Cash Flow to Firm (FCFF) or Unlevered CF = Operating CF - CAPEX + Interest Expense x (1-tax)

expression: Operating cash flow − cash CAPEX + net borrowing
original_wording: Free Cash Flow to Equity (FCFE) or Levered CF = Operating CF - CAPEX + Net Debt Proceeds

expression: Operating cash flow + compatible after-tax interest − cash CAPEX
original_wording: Free Cash Flow to the Firm = Operating Cash Flow + Interest x (1 - Tax Rate) + Changes in Fixed Assets

measure: FCFE: use changes, not balance totals
expression: Net income + noncash charges − cash CAPEX − increase in noncash operating working capital + net borrowing
original_wording: Free Cash Flow to Equity = Net Income + Depreciation and Amortisation + Accounts Receivables + Accounts Payable + Inventory Balances + Current Assets and Liabilities + CAPEX + Net Borrowing

expression: Inventory days + receivable days − payable days
original_wording:
Cash Conversion Cycle (CCC) = Days of Inventory Outstanding + Days of Sales Outstanding - Days of Payables Outstanding
The time to converts its inventory and receivables minus the time to pay its supplier. Low CCC means efficient management and has cash available to pay obligations and invest in growth opportunities.

expression: Average trade receivables / net credit sales × period days
original_wording:
Day Sales Outstanding (DSP) = Average Accounts Receivables / Net Credit Sales x 365
How long, on average, it takes for a company to collect payments from its customers for credit sales. A lower DSO indicates that the company is collecting its receivables more quickly.

expression: Average trade payables / credit purchases × period days
original_wording:
Days Payable Outstanding (DPO) = Average Accounts Payable / Purchases x 365
How long, on average, a company takes to pay its suppliers after receiving goods or services on credit. A higher DPO indicates that the company is taking longer to settle its payables, which can positively impact its cash flow and working capital.

expression: Average inventory / cost of goods sold × period days
original_wording:
Days Inventory Outstanding (DIO) = Average Inventory / CoGS x 365
How long, on average, it takes for a company to sell its inventory. Lower DIO indicates that the company is selling its inventory quickly and efficiently.

expression: DSO − best-possible DSO
original_wording:
Average Days Delinquent = Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) - Best Possible Days Sales Outstanding (BPDSO)
Measures effectiveness of collection efforts. Often used at client level to compare with the others

expression: Overdue receivables / total relevant receivables
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Overdues Ratio = Overdues / Total Receivables
Measures your effectiveness of collecting cash and the quality of your receivables

expression: Average inventory / annual COGS × 365
original_wording:
Days of Inventory Outstanding = Average Inventory / Yearly CoGS x 365
Average number of days that a company holds inventory for before turning it into sales

measure: Payable days using a COGS proxy
expression: Average trade payables / annual COGS × 365
original_wording:
Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) = Average Account Payables / Yearly CoGS X 365
Average number of days that it takes a company to pay its suppliers

expression: Operating cash flow / net sales
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Operating Cash Flow to Sales Ratio = Operating Cash Flow / Net Sales
Measures the percentage of each sales dollar that is converted into operating cash flow. A higher ratio indicates that a company is generating more operating cash flow per dollar of sales.

expression: Operating cash flow / current liabilities
original_wording:
Operating Cash Flow Ratio = Operating Cash Flow / Current Liabilities
Cash-generating capability relative to its revenue. Higher OCFR suggests that the company is generating a significant amount of cash from its core operations compared to its total revenue.

expression: Operating cash flow / current liabilities
original_wording:
Operating Cash Flow to Current Liabilities Ratio = Operating Cash Flow / Current Liabilities
Higher is generally better because it indicates that the company's operating cash flow is sufficient to cover its short-term obligations, which reflects a healthier financial position and reduced liquidity risk.

expression: Operating cash flow / average total assets
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Cash Flow Return on Assets (CFROA) = Operating Cash Flow / Average Total Assets
Higher is better because it indicates that the company is generating more cash flow from its assets, reflecting better operational efficiency and profitability. It shows how effectively the company is utilizing its assets to generate cash flow.

expression: Operating cash flow / net income
original_wording:
Cash Flow to Net Income = Operating Cash Flow / Net Income
Higher is generally better because it suggests that the company's reported net income is being supported by strong operating cash flows, which indicates the company's earnings are backed by actual cash generated from its operations rather than just accounting adjustments.

measure: Operating cash flow per common share
expression: (Operating cash flow − preferred cash dividends) / weighted-average common shares
original_wording:
Cash Flow per Share = (Operating Cash Flow - Perferred Dividends) / Weighted Average Number of Common Shares Outstanding
Higher is generally better as it indicates that each share of the company is generating more cash flow, which can be beneficial for shareholders.

measure: Cash flow to investors: unresolved definition
original_wording:
Cash Flow to Investors = Free Cash Flow - Net Debt Issued
Higher is generally good as it indicates the company is raising more capital or reducing debt through financing activities

expression: Cash available for debt service / scheduled principal and interest
original_wording:
Cash Debt Service Coverage Ratio (CDSCR) = Operating Cash Flow / Total Debt Service
Higher is better as it indicates that the company generates sufficient operating cash flow to cover its total debt service obligations, ensuring better ability to meet debt payments and reducing the risk of default.

measure: Simple FCF return on invested capital
expression: Free cash flow / invested capital
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording:
Cash Flow Return on Investment (CFROI) = Free Cash Flow / Invested Capital
Higher is better as it indicates a higher return on the initial investment after considering both operating cash flow generated and capital expenditures, which is a positive indicator of the investment's profitability.

expression: Available cash reserves / average daily relevant cash expenses
original_wording:
Cash Reserves in Days = Cash Reserves / Average Daily Expenses
Measures of how long your organisation could survive if cash dried up tomorrow

expression: Operating cash flow / net sales × 100
original_wording:
Cash Flow Margin = (Cash Flow from Operations / Net Sales) x 100
Measures your business's cash from operating activities as a percentage of your sale's revenue over a given period

expression: Defined free cash flow / net sales × 100
original_wording:
Free Cash Flow Margin = (Free Cash Flow / Neet Sales) x 100
Profitability ratio that compares a company's free cash flow to its revenue

expression: Cash available for debt service / (principal due + interest due)
original_wording:
Cash Flow Coverage Ratio = Cash Flow from Operations / (Principal + Interest)
Liquidity formula that shows the relationship between a company's total debt and operating cash flow

expression: Net sales / average defined working capital
original_wording:
Cash Conversion Efficiency (CCE) = Net Sales / Average Working Capital
A metric that expresses the length of time, in days, that it takes for a company to convert resources into cash flows

expression: Operating cash flow + investing cash flow
original_wording:
Cash Burn = Cash from Operating Activities + Cash from Investing Activities
Measures the amount of cash consumed without accounting for activities related to financing (equity / debt). A higher cash burn measn the company is consuming more money outside of activities related to financing.

expression: Included monthly cash outflows − included monthly cash inflows
original_wording:
Cash Burn Rate = Cash Spent (monthly average) - Cash Received (monthly average)
Net Cash spent by a company in a specific time frame (usually monthly or normalised to a year)

expression: Included cash outflows − included cash inflows
original_wording:
Net Burn Rate = Cash Spent - Cash Received
Net Cash spent by a company in a specific time frame (usually monthly or normalised to a year)

expression: Available cash / positive net burn per period
original_wording:
Runway = Current Cash Balance / Burn Rate
Time that a startup has before they run out of finance

expression: Latest monthly revenue × 12
original_wording:
Revenue Run Rate = The months revenue * 12
An annualised version of your revenue

expression: First forecast date when the cash balance reaches the stated depletion threshold
original_wording:
Cash Out Date = This month + Runway
Date in which you run out of cash

expression: Σ CFₜ / (1 + r)ᵗ
original_wording:
Discounted Cash Flow = CF1 / (1 + r)^1 + CF2 / (1 + r)^2 + ... + CFn / (1 + r)^n
Valuing an investment or a company by discounting its expected future cash flows to their present value. High DCF indicates the company is expected to generate more cash in the future.

measure: Present value of a single cash flow
expression: CF / (1 + r)ⁿ
original_wording:
Present Value = CF / (1 + r)^n
It measures the current value of a future cash flo, given a discount rate. A higher PV indicates that the future cash flow is more valuable today.

measure: Future value of a single amount
expression: PV × (1 + r)ⁿ
original_wording:
Future Value = PV * (1 + r)^n
FV measures the value of a current cash flow at a future point in time, given on interest rate. A higher FV indicates that the current cash flow will be worth more in the future.

expression: Initial investment / annual positive net cash inflow
original_wording:
Payback Period = Initial Investment / Annual Cash Flow
The payback period measures the amount of time it takes for an investment to generate enough cash flows.

expression: Next-period sustainable cash flow / (discount rate − long-run growth rate)
original_wording:
Terminal Value (TV) = (Free Cash Flow * (1 + Long-term Growth Rate)) / (Discount Rate - Long-term Growth Rate)
Analysis to estimate the value of a business or an investment beyond the explicit forecast period.

expression: Risk-free rate + equity beta × (expected market return − risk-free rate)
original_wording: Discount Rate = risk free rate + investment beta (market rate - risk free rate)

expression: After-tax operating profit − (compatible cost of capital × invested capital)
original_wording: Economic Value Added (EVA) = EBIT (1 - tax) - ((long term debt + equity) x WACC)

expression: (E / (D + E)) × rE + (D / (D + E)) × rD × (1 − tax rate)
original_wording: Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) = (E/V x Re) + ((D/V x Rd) x (1 - tax rate))

expression: After-tax operating profit / average defined operating invested capital
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording: Return on Invested Capital (RoIC) = EBIT (1 - tax) / (long term debt + equity - cash)

expression: Shares outstanding × market price per share
original_wording:
Market Value of Equity = Shares Outstanding x Market Price per Share
Total value of ownership in the company held by its shareholders

expression: Market capitalisation / book equity
original_wording:
Market-to-Book Ratio = Market Capitalisation / Book value of Equity
A company's stock is trading above or below its accounting value per share

expression: Equity market value + debt − cash
original_wording:
Enterprise Value = Market value of equity + Debt - Cash
The total value of a company

expression: Market price per share / book equity per corresponding share
original_wording:
Price-to-book ratio = Market Price per Share ​/ Book Value per Share
Compare a firm’s market to book value.

expression: Market price per share / compatible earnings per share
original_wording:
Price-to-Earnings (P/E) Ratio = Market Price Perer Share / EPS
The relationship between a company's stock price and its earnings per share.

expression: Purchase price = fair value of identifiable net assets + goodwill
original_wording: Purchase Price = Net Book Value + Fair Market Value Adjustments + Goodwill

expression: Defined EBITDA / matching revenue
units: ratio; multiply by 100 to express a percentage
original_wording: EBITDA Margin = EBITDA / Revenue

expression: EBITDA + separately identified signed adjustments
original_wording: Adjusted EBITDA = Net Income + Interest + Taxes + Depreciation/Amortisation + Adjustments

measure: EBITDA bridge: complete the split source line
expression: Net income + interest expense + income tax expense + depreciation + amortisation
original_wording:
Cross-verify with the formula: EBITDA = Net Income + Interest + Taxes +
Depreciation + Amortisation.

expression: Normalized eligible MRR × 12

ARRt = Total Monthly Recurring Revenue * 12
